channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Kano governor says his wife was taken from Government House before divorce filing
item.description: Abba Kabir Yusuf described how his wife left the Government House residence in Kano and later filed for divorce in Abuja.

item.title: Sierra Leone civil society group demands finance minister's dismissal
item.description: The Consortium on Public Accountability says hardship reflects poor inflation control and reckless borrowing, which a rebuttal disputes.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains families as tree loss threatens land
item.description: A government energy compact says only 15% of the population has access to clean cooking, while charcoal production removes trees.

item.title: Sierra Leone regulator reports NLE 7.4 million in 2024 revenue
item.description: The Sierra Leone Electricity and Water Regulatory Commission said levies and licences brought in the income, up from NLE 2.3 million in 2023.

item.title: Malawi airport tells passengers to arrive four hours early amid check-in fault
item.description: Kamuzu International Airport has used manual check-in since Nov. 17 after heavy rain and strong winds disrupted its automated service.

item.title: China gives Benin army CFA20 million in farm equipment
item.description: The machines are destined for women's village groups and cooperatives, with delivery to the field scheduled for the week of 7 December.

item.title: First-time buyers make up 48.5% of South African home-loan applications
item.description: Ooba data show first-time buyers averaged an 8.5% deposit, while approval rates reached 83.9% this year.

item.title: Emi Koussi wins Chad's national oratory contest by 0.05 point
item.description: The university scored 16.85 out of 20 in the final, edging the National Higher School of Information and Communication Technologies.

item.title: Central African authorities face questions over route to dissolve state body
item.description: Corbeau News Centrafrique questions whether the handling of a possible dissolution reflects legal uncertainty or the use of law for political ends.

item.title: Murkomen opens police hiring to observers at 423 centres
item.description: Kenya’s nationwide constable recruitment is scheduled for December 10, with applicants required to arrive by 8am.

item.title: Bondoukou youth council elects Ali Ouattara coordinator
item.description: The council, set up by NGO EVEIL-CI, gives youth groups a shared forum to make proposals and raise concerns with local authorities.

item.title: Libyan inspector says counterfeit medicines enter daily
item.description: Abu Bakr Marwan says his Souq Al-Jumaa team is short of resources and has spent seven years inspecting food and medicines.

item.title: Mauritius schedules seven football matches for Sunday
item.description: The third round of the 2026-2027 season includes fixtures in the National Super League, National Division Two and National Women’s Super League.

item.title: Rights group sues Nigeria's data regulator and electoral commission over AI-altered vot...
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project seeks a court order compelling an investigation into suspected AI-generated photographs in the voters' register.

item.title: CAF returns to profit with $31.2 million net surplus
item.description: Africa's football governing body books a $31.2 million net gain on $284 million in revenue, its first profit after years of financial strain.

item.title: KWS adds helicopter and drones to search for missing Aberdare hiker
item.description: The Kenya Wildlife Service says aerial equipment will help teams cover more ground in dense forest as they search for Elder David Kenneth Kihuna.

item.title: Stanbic Bank retains Uganda’s Bank of the Year title
item.description: The bank won four honours at Kampala’s 2nd Annual Bankers’ Awards, including Best Trade Finance Bank and two awards for its staff.

item.title: Adouma accuses Central African Republic president of nepotism
item.description: The opposition figure says family favoritism shapes senior appointments and blames the president for entrenched administrative failures.

item.title: Uganda signs 10-year crude marketing deal with Vitol
item.description: The trader will sell Pearl Sweet crude to international buyers and train the state oil company as exports are expected in early 2027.

item.title: Zambia reaffirms livelihood support for vulnerable households through its Food Security...
item.description: The government says the programme offers sustainable livelihood opportunities to improve household food security across the country.

item.title: Kogi soldiers seize two AK-47s in raid on bandit enclave
item.description: The army says its intelligence-led operation in Okehi was aimed at kidnap gangs behind recent abductions along the Kabba–Okene Road.

item.title: Government commissions K900,000 fashion hub and solar system at Chilanga school
item.description: Mount Makulu Secondary School received a furnished Fashion and Fabric Hub and a 16-kilowatt solar system, with foundation backing.

item.title: Guinea’s CBG receives ESG Gold 2026 award at Hanoi conference
item.description: The bauxite company received the award at the International Bauxite, Alumina & Aluminium Society’s 15th conference in October.

item.title: Standard & Poor's raises Zambia's sovereign rating to B-
item.description: The upgrade from CCC+/C carries a stable outlook, with the ratings agency citing debt-restructuring progress and sustained fiscal reforms.

item.title: Magwi access roads ease farmers’ route from fields to markets
item.description: Residents say a community road linking farming areas to the main route is helping vehicles carry produce without getting stuck.

item.title: Nigeria and China strengthen cultural ties through music
item.description: The Punch reports a music-based cultural effort between the two countries, but gives no details on participants, events or plans.

item.title: Ledama defends shooting threat over KSh365,000 employment claim
item.description: The Narok senator says alleged auctioneers entered a company linked to him and took the keys to its delivery truck under a court order.

item.title: Tunisia reviews appointments for vacant mosque posts
item.description: Religious Affairs Minister Ahmed Bouhali says candidates are assessed by regional commissions as his department works to shorten delays.

item.title: Adebayor urges Togo to qualify for Africa Cup of Nations
item.description: The former captain says the team must concentrate through the eliminators after missing several editions of the tournament.

item.title: King Tee Dee plans businesses and community projects to outlast his music
item.description: The Namibian musician, once known as The Dogg, says his shift in stage name reflects more experience and a wider vision.

item.title: Tunisia says alternative sentences exclude crimes
item.description: Justice Minister Leïla Jaffel told Parliament the measures apply only to eligible offences and require the convicted person’s consent.

item.title: Tunisia tourism executive Adel Boussarsar dies
item.description: The former head of Tunisie Voyages and founder of Golden Yasmine Hotels worked in Tunisian tourism from the 1970s through 2016.

item.title: Senegal sends music delegation to Rabat to pursue export markets
item.description: About 30 music professionals attended Visa For Music, where Senegalese acts performed and representatives explored links with foreign industry players.

item.title: Buyinza Adam urges NRM politicians to drop succession debate
item.description: The businessman says political organizing distracts citizens from wealth creation and efforts to reduce household poverty.

item.title: Abuja Iyoto Galy builds a rap career in Chad
item.description: The artist blends rap, trap and afro-drill, using music for expression and denunciation in a scene she describes as largely male.

item.title: Nandi-Ndaitwah urges youth to prepare for Dangote project contracts
item.description: The president says young businesses should build capacity and partnerships to compete for subcontracts on a planned N$42-billion tank farm and pipeline.

item.title: Auction of Hauwanga company assets puts 169 jobs at risk
item.description: The sale is tied to BH Spares Accessories Equipment and Technologies CC’s N$137 million debt to Bank Windhoek.

item.title: Namibia Air needs N$1.2 billion from government, study shows
item.description: A confidential study projects the proposed national airline will lose N$89 million in its first two years.

item.title: Diaspora group urges Sifuna to fund JKIA expansion without foreign investors
item.description: At a New Jersey meeting, a Kenyan in Ohio said overseas Kenyans could pool money and partner with the government to modernise the airport.

item.title: Libya ranks second in Africa for central bank gold reserves
item.description: Algeria leads the continent with 173.6 tonnes, and the top four holders together hold 575.8 tonnes, a World Gold Council tally cited in a 20 November report.

item.title: African Union launches Port-Louis credit agency; ratings due by March
item.description: The Africa Credit Rating Agency is in talks with 15 governments and plans research in Mauritius, Kenya, Togo, Seychelles and Burundi.

item.title: Paris colloquium outlines legal routes to pursue Wagner crimes
item.description: The March 2 gathering focused on crimes by Wagner and affiliates, including individual prosecutions and universal jurisdiction in third countries.

item.title: Central African Republic cabinet grants Green Mining two industrial mining permits
item.description: The permits were approved at the cabinet meeting of 23 July 2026, the latest in a run of concessions that the report says are handed out to private groups.

item.title: Eswatini pension funds’ combined quarterly surplus falls to E59.2 million
item.description: The Public Enterprises Unit links the decline from about E800 million to oil, energy and defence-stock volatility during the quarter.

item.title: Senegalese young reporters convene African media conference in Dakar
item.description: The 23-24 November gathering will examine how news organisations can fund journalism while preserving editorial independence.

item.title: Eswatini central bank holds discount rate at 7%
item.description: The decision keeps the prime lending rate at 10.50% as October inflation rises to 3.4%.

item.title: Bank of Mauritius sells $15 million as consumer advocate questions results
item.description: The November 18 sale brought its 2026 currency interventions to about $170 million, while the rupee lost 2.2% against the dollar from January to October.

item.title: Analyst questions Team Gambia's absence from opposition alliances
item.description: Political analyst Lamin Juwara says he expected the group to join a larger bloc before nominations for the December presidential election.

item.title: LUANAR honours biopesticide researcher at excellence awards
item.description: Dr Trust Donga’s natural pest-control formulations have cleared Malawi’s agricultural technology review and are in final registration.

item.title: University of Lomé schedules medical tests for new students
item.description: Students must register online and pay analysis fees at Ecobank before attending the 7 a.m. appointment on Monday, 23 November.

item.title: Gibba pledges salaries for all Gambian imams and Christian clergy
item.description: The No-To Alliance candidate says his administration would pay every imam, pastor and priest if elected in December 2026.

item.title: Mutharika gives K5 million to women journalists' association
item.description: The Association of Women in Media is holding its elective annual general meeting in Mponela, Dowa, where members are choosing new leaders.

item.title: Jospong subsidiary and Turkish firm begin Ghana farm-product trials
item.description: The research will test whether products made from discarded shrimp and crab shells protect crops, improve soil and offer farmers cheaper inputs.

item.title: Maka Masireh residents press candidates for roads and basic services
item.description: The remote Upper River Region village says a difficult road journey and limited local health care leave residents struggling to reach essential services.

item.title: Senegal's sanitation office blames roadworks for sewer disruptions
item.description: The National Sanitation Office (ONAS) says Dakar municipality repairs have buried or damaged inspection chambers, while the city mayor blames the agency for delayed works.

item.title: Moulay Rachid presides over Marrakech festival opening dinner
item.description: The prince, who leads the festival foundation, joined a dinner hosted by King Mohammed VI as the 23rd edition began.

item.title: Morocco meets Ghana in Amputee Football World Cup final
item.description: Morocco reached its first final by beating Brazil 2-1, overturning a one-goal deficit in a match decided late in the tournament.

item.title: Malawi's ruling party blames fuel shortages on US-Iran conflict
item.description: Jappie Mhango, vice-president of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) for the North, said the shortages stem from turmoil in the Middle East, not the party's own decisions.

item.title: Tunis medical students plan strike over exams and training conditions
item.description: The students’ organisation says the 23 November stoppage will press for an exam-calendar revision and a restart of internship appeals.

item.title: Ethiopia’s startup law opens incentives to foreign founders
item.description: Article 40 allows foreign startups and ecosystem builders to access incentives, while excluding foreign startups from the grant programme.

item.title: Ethiopian-born children report unequal access to citizenship
item.description: Some children of Ethiopian mothers and foreign fathers say they struggle to secure nationality, while another man obtained an identity card and passport without difficulty.

item.title: Ethiopia's ride-hailing sector pays 340 million birr in income tax
item.description: More than 30 platforms compete in Addis Ababa on fares and vehicle types, while 33,000 drivers, most of them self-employed, carry the costs of fuel and rent.

item.title: Exporters warn smuggling is undermining Ethiopia’s pulses and oilseeds trade
item.description: The exporters’ association says illegal channels are weakening formal sales as Ethiopia seeks to expand processing, quality and overseas markets.

item.title: Kamerhe urges Tshisekedi to review military strategy and spending
item.description: The former National Assembly president says the government should assess results and account for billions mobilised since the war began.

item.title: Abomey-Calavi mayor urges residents to stay clear of roadworks and reservoirs
item.description: Mayor Nathanaël D. Koty has published safety rules for the construction of rainwater reservoirs and nearby road projects.

item.title: Yambressinga urges Burkina Faso to replace municipal special delegations with revolutio...
item.description: The governance specialist says the appointed bodies have put routine administration ahead of investment and local development in the communes.

item.title: Vanderpuye proposes 1% salary fund for NDC workers’ pensions
item.description: The NDC chairmanship aspirant says he would negotiate with the President and Chief of Staff to secure contributions from government appointees.

item.title: Libya's state oil firm reports 30,792,522 USD loss from Hamada pipeline closure
item.description: The National Oil Corporation says an armed group's shutdown of the pipeline has cut crude output by 302,778 barrels over more than 20 days.

item.title: African guarantee fund plans sector-focused business fairs in Guinea
item.description: The fund says it will discuss further editions with Guinean authorities after the first event outside the West African monetary union.

item.title: Burkina Faso trains 99 retiring military personnel in farming and livestock
item.description: The graduates studied crop production and animal husbandry and pledged to start projects at a small scale before expanding them.

item.title: Mondlane tells court “take power” was meant to mobilise public
item.description: The Mozambican politician said the phrase referred to popular power and people’s ability to influence decisions.

item.title: Djibouti proposes permanent secretariat for African official gazettes
item.description: A forum is due to consider a cooperation charter, shared publication standards and a database for laws issued across the continent.

item.title: MUHAS draws more than 700 to health-awareness event
item.description: Participants from Tanzania and abroad took part in walks and runs promoting exercise, good nutrition and prevention of noncommunicable diseases.

item.title: Spain sends Morocco 170 files to return unaccompanied minors from Ceuta
item.description: Spanish police say the families of the children have been identified and have agreed to their return, but Rabat has not responded to any of the files.

item.title: Club Tamani looks at the veil that marks young Tuareg women's lives
item.description: Studio Tamani's programme traced where the practice began, when it starts in a girl's life and what it signifies in Tuareg society.

item.title: Comoros opens renovated lycée with library and science rooms
item.description: President Azali Assoumani inaugurated the Fomboni school on 21 November, thanking France and its development agency for supporting education.

item.title: Wazouna Déby Foundation gives food and hygiene kits to 300 households
item.description: The Chadian NGO distributed rice, oil, pasta, soap and mosquito nets in Machaga and Birbété to households identified with local leaders.

item.title: ProDAF supplies farm inputs to more than 350 Diffa-region producers
item.description: The package includes 10 tonnes of fertiliser, 80 litres of pesticides and seeds for rice, wheat, maize and vegetables.

item.title: Kara University project delivers three prototypes for rural farmers
item.description: Minodu developed irrigation, biopesticide and offline communication tools with communities in three localities over three years.

item.title: CAF raises annual payments to 54 member associations to 700 000 dollars
item.description: The increase follows a 31,2 million dollar net profit and a recovery from 16,8 million dollars in reserve deficits to a 14,4 million dollar surplus.

item.title: Benin’s foreign minister presents investment and AI priorities in Oslo
item.description: Corinne Amori Brunet urged alliances with local businesses and backed regulated artificial intelligence at a meeting of African and Nordic foreign ministers.

item.title: Rwasa files independent bid for Burundi’s 2027 presidency
item.description: The former National Congress for Liberty leader paid a 100 million-franc deposit and says he cannot obtain a required party-membership certificate.

item.title: Rwanda's EAX builds storage and quality systems to cut crop losses
item.description: The Kigali-based exchange has added warehouses, dryers and farmer training to help produce meet market standards and reach buyers.

item.title: Tanzania rally from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Costa Rica
item.description: Faraji Kayanda scored twice in the Serengeti Boys’ FIFA U17 World Cup debut in Doha, giving Tanzania a point in Group I.

item.title: Dakar health university puts counterfeit drugs and AI on 23 November agenda
item.description: The University of Health Sciences of Dakar will convene an international scientific day on medical training, patient safety and medicine quality.

item.title: Guinea's BCEIP sets sights on expanding beyond its borders
item.description: The 30-year-old company says it wants to deepen its contribution to Guinea's economy while extending its activities abroad.

item.title: Agama’s relegation decider delayed until November 25 after wage dispute
item.description: The Zimbabwe Premier Soccer League postponed both relegation fixtures after unpaid wages led Highlanders players to refuse travel and Agama’s squad to protest.

item.title: Chad equips six health facilities in Mandoul province
item.description: The health ministry handed medical-technical equipment to two district hospitals and four health centres serving four districts of the province.

item.title: CVsky adds flights to clear passengers disrupted by medical evacuations
item.description: The airline says about 92% of roughly 1,060 affected passengers were regularised by Friday, 20 November, after medical flights took priority.

item.title: Dollar reaches 248 dinars on Algeria’s parallel market
item.description: The rate at Algiers’ Port-Saïd exchange square matched the dollar’s record, while the euro held at 276 dinars.

item.title: Hardrock FC clinches Zimbabwe title in debut top-flight season
item.description: The Kwekwe side beat FC Platinum 1-0 at Chahwanda Stadium to finish on 73 points, two clear of Scottland FC.

item.title: Malawi motorists sleep at filling stations as fuel queues deepen
item.description: Drivers have reportedly spent days and nights waiting for fuel through October and November as shortages persist across the country.

item.title: Asiedu Nketiah says Asante regalia loans fall short of restitution
item.description: The NDC chairman says some royal objects displayed at the Manhyia Palace Museum remain on loan from British museums rather than transferred to community ownership.

item.title: Maniema authorities take control of Kindu medical oxygen plant
item.description: The World Bank-funded facility was handed to the provincial government more than a year after it was inaugurated.

item.title: Five Sierra Leone agribusinesses advance US$64 million financing pipeline
item.description: The firms met institutional financiers at the inaugural West African Integration and Investment Summit in Lungi; deals still require approvals and contracts.

item.title: Letter calls for citizens to control South Sudan dialogue agenda
item.description: The writer says a proposed Citizens’ Assembly needs independent conveners and representatives chosen by citizens, with leaders limited to presenting their views.

item.title: Chapo breaks ground on parliament building in 6,000-hectare city
item.description: The planned complex in Mocuba will also house MPs and staff, parliamentary studies and other economic and social infrastructure.

item.title: Djibouti City prefecture clears vehicles and levels roads in three districts
item.description: The campaign also cleaned the EEGA (Escale Ecologique Grand Arrosage) canal and its banks, with police, road-agency and company equipment supporting the work.

item.title: Miss Namibia unveils bee-eater costume for Miss Universe
item.description: The national costume is inspired by the Southern Carmine Bee-eater, a bird found along Namibia’s Zambezi River, and features crimson, teal and black colours.

item.title: Mali's cargo council reports nearly CFA80 billion in savings
item.description: Transport Minister Madina Sissoko said measures agreed with Dakar and Abidjan port authorities reduced or cancelled penalties on Malian goods.
